stops.title: The artist is in his studio
stops.story_quote: The painting's survival owes much to Chevalier Antoine de la Roque...who preserved the work through his collection
specifics_traced: Chevalier Antoine de la Roque, b.1672, provenance (confirmed, MFA collections record)
MFA Center for Netherlandish Art (real department)

stops.title: Madame Monet wearing a kimono
stops.story_quote: the critic Simon Boubée reviewed the painting and wrote that Monet 'has shown a Chinese in a red robe with two heads...'
specifics_traced: contemporary critics called the figure a 'demimondaine', a 'two-headed Chinese' (confirmed, MFA conservation page, close paraphrase)
2015 kimono try-on event and the controversy it caused (confirmed)

fabrications.claim: attributing the exact quoted review specifically to a named critic 'Simon Boubée'
fabrications.why: the MFA's own page attributes similar language to unnamed 'conservative critics' collectively; a specific named attribution could not be verified and may be invented

stops.title: Watson and the Shark
stops.story_quote: Copley introduced despite originally sketching only white figures...a detail Copley introduced
specifics_traced: 1749 Havana attack, 1778 painting, MFA original version (documented)
black sailor added in revision (documented via infrared/compositional study)
Watson became Lord Mayor/Alderman of London (documented)

stops.title: Dance at Bougival
stops.story_quote: When Félix François Depeaux bought Dance at Bougival from Paul Durand-Ruel in 1894, he promised to eventually give it to the Musée de Rouen...he later needed money to finance a costly divorce
specifics_traced: Depeaux was a real Rouen-based collector and major donor of Impressionist works (documented)
Durand-Ruel was the dealer (documented, per MFA provenance)

fabrications.claim: the specific 1894 purchase date, the promise to the Musée de Rouen, and the divorce motive for selling
fabrications.why: MFA's own provenance record shows a different, more convoluted ownership chain (deposited/returned/sold through Durand-Ruel in the 1880s) with no mention of Depeaux, Rouen, or a divorce; this looks like an invented, overly tidy causal story

stops.title: Bocca Baciata
stops.story_quote: Rossetti's choice of Fanny Cornforth as the model...lends a quiet, personal gravity
specifics_traced: Rossetti, 1859, oil on panel, Fanny Cornforth model (documented)
letter to William Bell Scott about the stippling fault (documented anecdote)

stops.title: Fray Hortensio Félix Paravicino
stops.story_quote: He argued for the destruction of all nude paintings, believing their existence threatened moral order
specifics_traced: Paravicino was a Trinitarian friar, poet, orator (documented)

fabrications.claim: Paravicino 'argued for the destruction of all nude paintings'
fabrications.why: no source found tying this specific extreme position to Paravicino; looks invented to manufacture dramatic conflict

defects: Depeaux/divorce story contradicts the MFA's own provenance record
Calls the MFA's full-scale replica the 'large, original version' (original is NGA Washington)
one_line_verdict: Strong D511 story count (5/6) and mostly real specifics, but a fabricated/overwritten provenance anecdote at stop 4 and an invented position at stop 6.
